title: Transportation Agencies Breakdown World Cup Performance 8/26/2026
description:
Los Angeles is racing against the clock to build a transportation system capable of moving millions of people during the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

During a congressional panel in West Hollywood, federal lawmakers and regional transportation leaders examined lessons from the 2026 FIFA World Cup and the challenges that remain before LA28. Metro’s enhanced World Cup bus service provided more than 212,000 rides to and from SoFi Stadium, offering an important preview of the planning, coordination and public-safety measures required for a global sporting event.

The discussion addressed the need for approximately 1,700 additional buses, billions of dollars in federal support and greater coordination among Metro, LADOT, municipal transit agencies and public-safety partners. Officials also discussed traffic congestion, first- and last-mile connections, accessibility, bicycle parking, rideshare services, neighborhood impacts and the need to protect everyday transit service for local residents.

Leaders emphasized that transportation investments made for LA28 should create lasting benefits—including safer streets, improved bus stops, better mobility infrastructure and new economic opportunities—for communities across the Los Angeles region.
